plan: G-6 false positive: a read-only grep whose quoted argument contains a trade or deployment pattern was flagged as a send. Step 1 of 2 (this PR): the gate fix in ci/gates/check_rollback.py only. Step 2 (bot-02-risk/v4-p11-g6-grep-selftests, after this PR merges) re-adds the red-green self-tests.
purpose: Receipt for step 1 of a two-step G-6 fix. find_matches now matches patterns against the command with the operands of a simple read-only search command (grep, egrep, fgrep, zgrep, zegrep, zfgrep) blanked out. The mask is applied only when the command has no expansion, newline, comment or unterminated quote, so a command that runs cannot hide behind a grep. The trade pattern for on-chain sends also accepts the camelCase form, which it previously missed. This PR adds no test: the trusted gate-self-test runs this PR's tests against main's gate scripts, so a test that depends on the fix must wait for step 2. The self-test cases written for this fix are in commit 1c97253 and are not in this PR.

Reverting restores the earlier false positives on grep arguments and the missed camelCase sendTransaction; no ledger, live state or runtime behaviour changes. Expected recovery time: about 5 minutes.

A command such as grep x docs | sh is not flagged, because no destructive or deployment pattern names sh; this was already true before the change and is unchanged.
The mask does not apply to ripgrep, ag or ack, because rg --pre runs a command per file. Commands with those tools are matched in full.
A grep command with an unescaped $ or backtick, a newline, a comment or an unterminated quote is matched in full. This fails closed, so such a receipt can still be flagged for quoting a pattern.
Compound identifiers such as sendTransactionBatch are not matched by the trade pattern, which keeps the trailing word boundary used by the other trade patterns.
